items.title: Don Alias interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: I say when are you guys going to acknowledge Jaco Pastorius? You know we had a monumental concert for him at the Lone Star, you know Paul McCartney showed up and Sting showed up and those guys will tell you about Jaco.

ctx.x: More like some of the Rock ‘n Roll people that you read about who self destruct.

Yeah. He did that. It was almost like he was destined to go out early. You know he came, he was that spark that burned real bright and then disappeared. Now I’m like every time I meet anybody that’s associated with any kind of Grammy thing I always drop that on them. I say when are you guys going to acknowledge Jaco Pastorius? You know we had a monumental concert for him at the Lone Star, you know Paul McCartney showed up and Sting showed up and those guys will tell you about Jaco. I mean why don’t you have like…

What was it about his sound? I mean aside from all the beautiful technical, amazing technical stuff he did it was like one note, he had this particular sound. Was there equipment behind that? Was there something about his bass or was it just him?
